deadlineDefinition.title: Termijn Definitie
deadlineDefinition.description: Versioned deadline definition for a zaaktype under the AWB. Sets standard duration, allowed extensions, pause regime, and any custom dwangsom regime (e.g. Woo €15/day max €500).

caseType.title: Case Type
caseType.description: Zaaktype slug this definition binds to (e.g. omgevingsvergunning-regulier)

countingMode.title: Counting mode
countingMode.description: Whether this term counts every day or only the days the organisation works. An Awb beslistermijn counts calendar days, which is why that is the default and why shipping this property moves no date anybody is already counting on. A service norm, an internal handling term and a KCC callback count working days, and until now they could not. The working days are the organisation calendar's, not a list dossiq keeps, and the armed timer carries the same mode so the badge and the engine count down to one date.

rollToWorkingDay.title: Roll to the next ordinary day
rollToWorkingDay.description: When on, a term whose end date falls on a Saturday, Sunday or recognised holiday ends on the next ordinary day instead, as the Algemene termijnenwet requires. The days it moves over are the organisation calendar's, not a list dossiq keeps. On by default, because Awt art. 1 applies by law and not by configuration: the switch exists to turn the roll OFF for a term the Awt does not govern, which is the same reading TermijnTimerService::rollEnabled() has always had for a definition that carries no flag.

extensionCapacity.title: Extension Allowance Days
extensionCapacity.description: Maximum days a single AWB 4:14 verlenging may add

pauseExtensionDuration.title: Pause Extension Durations
pauseExtensionDuration.description: Allowed pause durations in days (e.g. AWB 4:5 hersteltermijn)

deviatingPenaltyPaymentRegime.title: Custom Penalty Regime
deviatingPenaltyPaymentRegime.description: Custom dwangsom regime overriding the AWB-default (€23/€35/€45 tiers, €1442 plafond)

dailyTariff.title: Daily Tariff
dailyTariff.description: Flat daily tariff in EUR cents (e.g. 1500 = €15)

grace.title: Grace Period Days
grace.description: Grace period in days before accrual starts (default 14)

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Which clock this definition sets. A first-response term is the promise every service desk makes, that you hear from us within so many days, and it is an ordinary term rather than a second mechanism. An absent value reads as statutory, because every definition written before the kinds existed is one.

organisation.title: Organisation
organisation.description: The organisation this term is agreed with. A gemeenschappelijke regeling runs one case type for five municipalities that agreed different norms, and without this the case type has to be duplicated five times and drifts. Empty means the term is the case type's own.

service.title: Service
service.description: The service this term belongs to, for a case type offered at more than one service level. Empty means it applies to every service.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: The derived priority this term applies to, read from the case's own priority (REQ-PRI-02) and never from a second priority field. Empty means it applies at every priority.

runsInStatuses.title: Runs in statuses
runsInStatuses.description: The statuses this clock runs in. In any other status the engine timer is suspended, and resuming moves the end date by what was banked, so a case sitting with an external adviser does not burn the same clock as one on a handler's desk. An empty list means the clock runs in every status, which is how every term behaved before this was declarable.

escalationLadder.title: Escalation ladder
escalationLadder.description: The rungs this term escalates on, each either a number of days before the end or a share of the whole term. A share is resolved to a date when the timer is armed, so the engine ladder stays the ladder and dossiq adds no second escalation. A quarter of a six-week term and a quarter of a twenty-six-week term mean the same thing to a handler and different dates to the timer, which is the point.

message.title: Message
message.description: What the escalation says when this rung is reached.

days.title: Days before the end
days.description: How many days before the end of the term this rung fires. Set this or a share, not both.

share.title: Share of the term elapsed
share.description: How much of the term must have elapsed before this rung fires, as a fraction between 0 and 1. Resolved to a date when the timer is armed.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: The priority the case takes when this rung fires.

validFrom.title: Valid From
validFrom.description: Definition takes effect on this date

validUntil.title: Valid Until
validUntil.description: Definition stops applying on this date; null = current version

deadlineInstance.title: Termijn Instance
deadlineInstance.description: Live deadline instance bound to a specific zaak. Tracks the original computed end date, the actual (mutable) end date after pauses and extensions, and the current status.
deadlineInstance.x-notes: `deadlineDefinition` left the required list in 1.1.0. Four kinds of clock are instances of this schema now, and only the statutory one materialises from a TermijnDefinitie: a planned end, an internal target and a phase term are declared on the case type and the status type. Keeping the reference required would have forced a made-up definition id onto three of the four kinds, which is worse than an absent reference because a made-up id resolves to nothing while claiming to resolve.

case.title: Case Reference
case.description: Reference to the dossiq case (case id)

kind.title: Kind of clock
kind.description: Which of the four clocks this is. The statutory term is the one the Awb sets and the citizen is told about. The planned end is the service norm your team steers on. The internal target is the teamleider's own number and never reaches a citizen. A phase term runs inside the case term for one phase. Each is warned on and reported separately, and none of them moves another.

statusType.title: Phase
statusType.description: The phase this clock belongs to. Filled in on a phase term and empty on the other three kinds.

plannedStartDate.title: Planned start date
plannedStartDate.description: The day work on this case is planned to start. A case carrying one shows it in the working list, so a handler can see what is coming as well as what is due.

deadlineDefinition.title: Deadline Definition Reference
deadlineDefinition.description: Reference to the TermijnDefinitie this instance materialised from

endDateCalculated.title: Calculated End Date
endDateCalculated.description: Original computed deadline (never mutated; used for audit)

endDateCurrent.title: Effective End Date
endDateCurrent.description: Effective deadline after pauses and extensions

pauseDeadline.title: Pause Deadline
pauseDeadline.description: Outstanding pause deadline for the daily scan to watch

relevantIngbrekes.title: Relevant Default Notice
relevantIngbrekes.description: Reference to the first valid Ingebrekestelling (one-dwangsom guard)

notificatiesVerstuurd.title: Notifications Sent
notificatiesVerstuurd.description: Threshold bucket numbers already notified (14/7/2/0) to prevent duplicate escalation

engineTimerId.title: Engine Timer Id
engineTimerId.description: Uuid of the OpenRegister FlowTimer that measures this term

pauseTimerId.title: Pause Timer Id
pauseTimerId.description: Uuid of the advisory FlowTimer that watches the hersteltermijn while the term is suspended

pauzeDuurDagen.title: Pause Duration Days
pauzeDuurDagen.description: Requested duration of the running pause in days

voltooiDatum.title: Completion Date
voltooiDatum.description: Date the term was completed by the beschikking

clockStoppedByStatus.title: Clock stopped by status
clockStoppedByStatus.description: Whether this term's clock is currently stopped because the case sits in a status the term does not run in. Written only by the status clock, and read only by it: an opschorting under Awb 4:5 is a different suspension with a different reason, and resuming one must never resume the other.

resolvedFrom.title: Resolved from
resolvedFrom.description: Which declaration produced this term. A term somebody disputes has to be explainable a year later, and the configuration will have changed by then, so the resolution is recorded rather than re-derived.

resolutionSnapshot.title: Resolution snapshot
resolutionSnapshot.description: What the resolution was made from, copied at the moment it was made. The explanation of a term must not depend on the configuration as it stands now: that is the whole reason this is a copy and not a reference.

caseType.title: Case type
caseType.description: The case type the term was resolved for.

organisation.title: Organisation
organisation.description: The organisation the term was resolved for.

service.title: Service
service.description: The service the term was resolved for.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: The priority the term was resolved for.

durationDays.title: Duration in days
durationDays.description: How many days the resolved term runs for.

deadlineDefinition.title: Definition
deadlineDefinition.description: The definition that produced this term.

resolvedAt.title: Resolved on
resolvedAt.description: The moment the term was resolved.

termijnGebeurtenis.title: Termijn Gebeurtenis
termijnGebeurtenis.description: Immutable append-only audit log entry for any termijn lifecycle event. Once written, never updated.

items.title: What was asked for
items.description: The missing items named in a request to the applicant, or the ones that came back with the aanvulling. Asking and suspending the term are one act under Awb 4:5, so one record carries what was asked, when it was asked, and the suspension it caused.

actor.title: Actor Reference
actor.description: User id or system process that triggered the event

daysImpact.title: Days Impact
daysImpact.description: Net effect on einddatumActueel in days (e.g. +14 for pauze, +28 for verleng)

documentLink.title: Document Link
documentLink.description: Reference to the supporting document (e.g. Verlengingsbrief)

noticeOfDefault.title: Ingebrekestelling
noticeOfDefault.description: Burger notice that the deadline has lapsed (AWB 4:17). Validated against the TermijnInstance to start a DwangsomBerekening.

gevalideerd.title: Validated
gevalideerd.description: Whether the notice was validated against the lapsed deadline

decisionRegisteredDate.title: Decision Registration Date
decisionRegisteredDate.description: Date the beschikking was filed (closes the grace period if before)

documentLink.title: Document Link
documentLink.description: Reference to the scanned notice PDF

penaltyPaymentCalculation.title: Dwangsom Berekening
penaltyPaymentCalculation.description: Daily-accruing dwangsom calculation per AWB 4:17. Tracks current day, tariff tier, cumulative amount in EUR cents, plafond enforcement.

startDate.title: Start Date
startDate.description: First accrual day (= ontvangstDatum + 14d grace, unless regime overrides)

cumulativeAmount.title: Cumulative Amount
cumulativeAmount.description: Total accrued so far in EUR cents

plafondBereikt.title: Ceiling Reached
plafondBereikt.description: True when the plafond has been hit; no further accrual

definitiveAmount.title: Final Amount
definitiveAmount.description: Locked final amount in EUR cents once stopped

dwangsomUitbetaling.title: Dwangsom Uitbetaling
dwangsomUitbetaling.description: Payment signal towards the burger after the dwangsom is locked.

accountHolderName.title: Account Holder Name
accountHolderName.description: Full name of the bank account holder receiving the payment

paymentDateLatest.title: Payment Deadline
paymentDateLatest.description: Deadline by which payment must occur (= ontvangstDatum + 28d)

actualPaymentDate.title: Actual Payment Date
actualPaymentDate.description: Date on which the payment was actually made
